---
title: The full form, defineIntegration
description: Widgets, actions, tools and images in one file.
sidebar: { order: 3 }
---

Use this when `service()` isn't enough: several widgets, buttons, or tools that change things.

An integration is one object. `create` gets the checked config and a context, and returns what the integration offers.

```js title="data/integrations/shelf-light.mjs"
export default ({ z, defineIntegration }) => defineIntegration({
  type: 'shelf-light',
  name: 'Shelf light',
  config: z.object({ url: z.string().url(), token: z.string() }).strict(),
  create(cfg, ctx) {
    const headers = { Authorization: `Bearer ${cfg.token}` };
    const state = () => ctx.http(`${cfg.url}/state`, { headers });
    const set = on => ctx.http(`${cfg.url}/state`, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify({ on }), as: 'text' });
    return {
      widgets: {
        light: {
          title: 'Shelf light', interval: 30_000,
          async fetch() {
            const s = await state();
            return { type: 'controls', title: 'Shelf light', icon: 'bulb',
              items: [{ id: 'power', label: 'Power', kind: 'toggle', value: s.on, action: 'power' }],
              summary: { label: 'Shelf light', icon: 'bulb', value: s.on ? 'On' : 'Off' } };
          },
        },
      },
      actions: {
        power: { description: 'Turn the shelf light on or off', input: z.object({ value: z.boolean() }),
          run: ({ value }) => set(value).then(() => ({ done: value ? 'Turned the shelf light on' : 'Turned the shelf light off' })) },
      },
      tools: {
        light_status: {
          label: 'Checked the shelf light', access: 'read', input: z.object({}),
          description: 'Whether the shelf light is on.',
          async run() { const s = await state(); return { data: s }; },
        },
        light_set: {
          label: 'Changed the shelf light', access: 'control', input: z.object({ on: z.boolean() }),
          description: 'Turn the shelf light on or off.',
          confirm: ({ on }) => ({ title: `Turn the shelf light ${on ? 'on' : 'off'}?`, icon: 'bulb', verb: on ? 'Turn on' : 'Turn off' }),
          async run({ on }) { await set(on); return { data: { on } }; },
        },
      },
    };
  },
});
```

As a built-in, it's the same with `import { z } from 'zod'` and `import { defineIntegration } from '../server/core.ts'`, and a line in `src/integrations/index.ts`.

## The parts

| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `type` | The `type:` in `config.yaml`. |
| `name` | Its name, shown to the assistant and in logs. |
| `config` | A zod schema. Valet checks the block against it and reports errors with the path. |
| `create(cfg, ctx)` | Returns the instance below. |

The instance:

| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `widgets` | Named cards for the page. Required, even if it's `{}`. |
| `actions` | What the page's controls and buttons can do. |
| `tools` | What the assistant can use. |
| `commands` | Plain words for ⌘K that run an action or a tool with no model. See [below](#commands). |
| `image(ref, range)` | Serves pictures. See [below](#images). |
| `recap(range)` | [Slides](/build/recap/) for the year in review. |
| `backups()` | Its [backup jobs](/build/backups/), for the Backups card. |
| `onChat()` | Called when someone asks the assistant something. Returns the widgets to refresh right away. |

## Widgets

A widget has a `title`, an optional `interval` in milliseconds, and `fetch()`, which returns a [card](/cards/).

- `interval` is how often it refreshes while someone's looking. 10 seconds by default.
- A widget not in the layout is never polled.
- Throw with a clear message when it fails: `throw new Error('qBittorrent login failed')`. It shows on the card.
- Give every card a `summary`, so it works at the small size, in the menubar and as a tile. The layout chooses the size, not the integration.
- Set `activity` on a card only while something's live, and it shows as a [ring in the top bar](/concepts/layout/#live-activities).

## Actions

An action has a `description`, an `input` schema and `run(args)`. A card names it from a `controls` item, or from `buttons`.

Valet checks the input, runs the action, and refreshes that integration's widgets. If the page is [read-only](/start/sign-in/), the action is refused.

An action may return `{ done: 'Archived a saved link' }`. That's what the activity log says it did, in place of the integration and action name.

## Tools

| Field | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `description` | yes | Written for the model: what it returns, when to use it. |
| `access` | yes | `read`, `write` or `control`. See [access levels](/assistant/access/). Pick the narrowest. |
| `input` | yes | A zod schema. |
| `run(args)` | yes | Returns `{ data, card }`. `data` goes to the model. `card` is what the person sees. |
| `label` | | What it did, past tense, for its chip in chat: "Searched documents". |
| `followUps` | | A couple of next questions to offer. |
| `find` | | The input field that takes search words. The tool then joins `search_everything` and ⌘K's search as you type, which draws its rows from the card: give items an `href` to open. |
| `nearest` | | With `find`: it always finds something, however far off (a search by likeness). Its rows go under the others' in ⌘K. |
| `live` | | Its card stays current in chat. Only for cheap, look-only tools whose answer changes by itself. |
| `confirm(input)` | | What the approval card says. See [confirm words](/build/confirm/). |
| `undo` | | The tool that reverses this one, given the same input. |

Keep `data` small, because the model's context is limited. Summarise, and don't return the raw API response.

Choosing the level:

- `read` only looks.
- `write` adds something the person asked for. Every call asks first.
- `control` changes or removes something. Every call asks first.

## Commands

Plain words for the [palette](/concepts/layout/#the-palette) that run an action or a tool by rule, with no model. Typing one exactly runs it.

```ts
commands: [
  { say: ['pause downloads', 'pause {name}'], run: 'action:pause', label: 'Pause all downloads' },
  { say: ["what's downloading", 'downloads'], run: 'tool:downloads_status' },
  { say: ['pause ads {minutes} min'], run: 'action:pause', label: 'Pause ad blocking: {minutes} min' },
],
```

| Field | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `say` | yes | Every phrasing you'd accept. `{name}` is the instance's name in `config.yaml`, or the integration's. `{minutes}` or any other slot takes a whole number and goes into the input under that name. |
| `run` | yes | `action:<name>` runs a page action, as its button would. `tool:<name>` runs a tool: a `read` one shows its card, anything else asks with its `confirm` words first. |
| `input` | | Fixed input, or a function of the slots. It may look things up, never change them, and may throw to say why it can't run now. |
| `label` | | What the palette shows. `{slot}` in it is filled in. The first phrase if left out. |

Matching ignores case, punctuation, word order, plurals and filler words ("the", "all", "please", "turn"), and a few words mean the same: off and disable, on and enable, pause and stop, resume, start and continue, min and minutes. Nothing else is guessed, so write the variants out. Two commands with the same words are both shown, and neither runs until one is picked.

`commands` can be a function, asked each time the palette opens. Home Assistant uses that to name every light it may control.

A command passes the same checks as the chat: a [read-only page](/start/sign-in/) only looks, a tool needs the [access](/assistant/access/) the assistant would need, input is checked by the target's schema, results are redacted, and anything that changes something goes in the activity log.

## Context

`create` gets `ctx`:

| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ctx.id` | The instance's key in `config.yaml`. |
| `ctx.format` | The config's `format:`, for a service that can answer in the right units. |
| `ctx.http(url, init)` | Fetch with a timeout (8 seconds by default) and a readable error. Parses JSON. Takes `as: 'text'` or `as: 'response'`, `timeout`, and `insecure` for a self-signed certificate. |
| `ctx.log(...)` | Logs with the instance's name. |
| `ctx.image(ref)` | The URL for a picture from your `image()`. |
| `ctx.upload(id)` | A file the person attached in chat. |
| `ctx.session(login)` | One sign-in shared by parallel calls. `.get()` for the token, `.reset()` after a 401. |

## Images

Put `ctx.image(ref)` in a card, and fetch it in `image()`. The browser never gets the key.

```js
image(ref) {
  if (!/^\d+$/.test(ref)) throw new Error('bad image ref');
  return ctx.http(`${cfg.url}/covers/${ref}.jpg`, { as: 'response', headers });
},
```

- **Validate `ref` first.** It comes from the browser. Accept only the shape you expect, and never treat it as an address.
- Return a `Response`. Only pictures and MP4 or WebM video get through. See [the image proxy](/security/image-proxy/).
- A picture that changes needs `Cache-Control: no-store` on the response, or the browser keeps it for a day.
- For video, `image(ref, range)` gets the browser's `Range` header. Phones won't play a video from a server that ignores it.

## Formatting

`fmt` keeps numbers the same everywhere: `fmt.bytes`, `fmt.rate`, `fmt.speed`, `fmt.duration`, `fmt.pct`, `fmt.day`, `fmt.time` and `fmt.relativeDay`.

## Rules of thumb

- One request per refresh if you can. If several widgets share data, fetch once and cache briefly.
- Don't invent card types. If the catalog lacks something, open an issue, because a new type works for everyone.
- Icons in cards are names, such as `cpu`, `disk`, `film`, or an image URL.
